methodological_rigor.justification: The study deploys an exceptionally layered experimental approach: FGF4-guided brainstem organoids validated against HNOCA and HDBCA reference atlases, in situ electroporation of H3.3K27M/DNp53/PDGFRA-D842V with appropriate empty-plasmid controls and an unguided cerebral organoid counterfactual, TrackerSeq lineage tracing, orthotopic NSG transplantation, methylation benchmarking against DMG/GBM/PFA, and scRNA-seq across tumor, CAR T, and microglia compartments. Quantitative readouts span multiple independent batches (e.g., n=84 organoids across time points, n=139 BrOs for electroporation timing, n=14 DMGOs across four batches) with donor-matched mock-transduced T cell controls and NCAM1+/- sorting experiments. Limitations are transparently acknowledged (hES/iPSC-derived postnatal tissue limits, absence of assembloid cross-regional interactions, CAR T n=1-4 DMGOs for some conditions). Statistically, the authors use two-tailed t-tests, one-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD, a linear mixed-effects model for repeated organoid measurements with FDR correction, and report exact P values; however, they explicitly did not predetermine sample size or formally test normality, and treatment-response comparisons rely on small n (1-6 DMGOs per arm), limiting power.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: As a preclinical de novo organoid model with mechanistic dissection of CAR T heterogeneity, exhaustion, and microglia-mediated immunosuppression, the study maps to Oxford LoE 5 (mechanistic/basic science). Clinical relevance is nonetheless strong: it directly interrogates GD2 CAR T cells used in recent DMG trials (Majzner 2022, Monje 2025), mirrors clinically observed heterogeneous responses, identifies NCAM1+ as an actionable selection marker for potent serial-killer CAR T cells, and implicates microglia as a resistance driver and IL-6/IL-1alpha-linked toxicity mediator. Findings inform near-term therapy composition strategies and preclinical platforms but are not themselves practice-changing without in vivo/clinical validation.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is the closest applicable standard given the murine orthotopic transplant experiments; the paper reports housing conditions, licensing (AVD39900 202216507), anesthesia, humane endpoints, sex/age of NSG mice, and perfusion protocols, with IRB approval (registry 2020.142) for patient material. Methods for organoid generation, electroporation parameters, scRNA-seq preprocessing (scDblFinder, Seurat v4, thresholds), methylation normalization (ChAMP, minfi, BMIQ), and statistical tests are explicit, though the authors note investigators were not blinded and sample sizes were not predetermined. A Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced. Data availability: protocols deposited on protocols.io, processed transcriptomic datasets on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.15356013), Supplementary Tables 1-10 with antibodies/gene lists/DEGs, and extensive source data per figure; raw sequencing repository is not explicitly stated in the provided text, preventing a 5.

novelty_literature.justification: The work introduces an FGF4-driven brainstem-regionalized organoid (distinct from prior midbrain/cerebellum/spinal cord protocols) and uses it for de novo H3.3K27M DMG genesis with pons-specific OPC-like 2/3 states, lineage-traced clonality, and months-long CAR T functional interrogation including a microglia-integrated tumor microenvironment. While H3K27M iPSC/hESC modeling (Funato 2014, Haag 2021, Bressan 2021), in utero electroporation mouse models (Pathania, Patel), and emerging DMG organoid platforms (Sarnow 2025, Deligne 2025) exist, the combination of brainstem regionalization, de novo tumorigenesis, prolonged CAR T heterogeneity mapping, NCAM1 sorting, and microglia co-integration fills a documented gap rather than providing incremental confirmation. It stops short of a first-in-class mechanistic discovery because each component has precedent, so a 4 rather than 5 is warranted.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured with logical flow from organoid characterization through tumor induction, clonal dynamics, CAR T heterogeneity, NCAM1 selection, and microglia integration. Figures are extensively annotated with sample sizes, statistical details, and methodological context, and the discussion honestly delineates limitations (postnatal maturation, intraregional interactions) and future directions (assembloids, retrograde tracing). Terminology is precise, acronyms are defined on first use, and the abstract accurately reflects the body. Prose is dense but publication-ready at a high-tier journal level.

key_strengths: Novel FGF4-driven brainstem organoid with rigorous benchmarking against HNOCA and HDBCA atlases showing pons/medulla glial enrichment (13 of 19 gained clusters)

De novo H3.3K27M/DNp53/PDGFRA DMG induction validated by methylation profiling, iCNV analysis, scRNA-seq mapping to primary DMG, and TrackerSeq lineage tracing demonstrating glial-specific clonal expansion

Prolonged (>1 month) CAR T functional dissection in tumor tissue context, identifying nine transcriptional states including antigen-driven TEX with tissue-residency features and NCAM1+ TCYT super-engager population

Microglia integration via PMPs reproducing DMG-specific immunosuppressive phenotype (CD163, SPP1) and demonstrating reduced CAR T tumor control with a novel TMA cluster, plus IL-6/IL-1alpha cytokine upregulation relevant to clinical neurotoxicity
Appropriate statistical treatment including linear mixed-effects models with FDR correction, and extensive source data with Zenodo/protocols.io deposition
key_concerns: Several pivotal comparisons rely on very small sample sizes (n=1-4 DMGOs per arm for CAR T treatment, n=2 DMGOs for NCAM1+/- sorting), with no predetermined sample-size calculation and normality assumed but not tested
Investigators were not blinded to allocation during experiments or outcome assessment, introducing possible measurement bias in imaging-based tumor quantification
Raw sequencing data repository (e.g., GEO/ENA) is not explicitly stated in the provided text; only processed data on Zenodo and protocols on protocols.io are referenced
Model inherently cannot capture postnatal tissue maturation, cross-regional neuronal circuits, or adaptive immunity, limiting translational generalization of microglia/CAR T findings
Microglia-CAR T treatment comparisons yielded borderline FDR-adjusted P values (t10 P=0.084, t14 P=0.058), which temper the strength of the resistance claim
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a technically ambitious, methodologically rigorous, and translationally relevant organoid platform paper with de novo DMG modeling, prolonged CAR T functional dissection, and microglia integration suitable for a top-tier oncology or broad-interest journal; minor revisions addressing small-n caveats, blinding, and explicit raw data deposition would suffice at tier 1.
